verdict.rationale: CockroachDB documents PostgreSQL compatibility: it speaks the Postgres wire protocol so existing Postgres drivers connect, and its VECTOR type is compatible with pgvector. However, it is a reimplementation rather than the Postgres engine itself, and a hands-on community report cites missing Postgres features (array columns), so it delivers a compatible subset rather than real engine parity. Missing for 10: evidence of full Postgres dialect/extension parity, a documented compatibility matrix, MySQL/SQLite dialect support, and current independent confirmation that gaps such as array columns are closed.

support.subject: As a developer, I get real engine compatibility — the Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite dialect and extensions my existing code expects — not a lookalike subset

citations.quote: CockroachDB supports the PostgreSQL wire protocol, so you can use any available PostgreSQL client drivers to connect from various languages.
CockroachDB is a cloud-agnostic, PostgreSQL compatible database built for modern applications
`VECTOR` functionality is compatible with the [`pgvector`](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) extension for PostgreSQL.
